"What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. A full e2e run builds its own fixturenet from the tree under test and runs every end-to-end job on that fixturenet, while the shared fixturenet at ~/deployments/armada-fixturenet-e12 keeps running. Each job reaches only the chain of its own deployment.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. Audit on integrated d51ae19, searched: stack/compose-jobs/*.yml, stack/scripts/*, env/gates/watchtower/*.ts, and the generated spec of the shared fixturenet. Published host ports: the spec maps geth to 127.0.0.1:8545:8545 and 127.0.0.1:8546:8546, and the beacon to 127.0.0.1:5052:5052 (~/deployments/armada-fixturenet-e12/spec.yml, network.ports). stack/scripts/fixturenet-new:113-116 runs `laconic-so deploy init --map-ports-to-host localhost-same`, which writes that spec. Port 8546 and port 5052 appear in none of the searched files. Host-address uses of port 8545 (127.0.0.1:8545 or localhost:8545): stack/scripts/fixturenet-new:30, stack/scripts/fixturenet-base-snapshot:29, stack/scripts/armada-watchtower-e2e.py:21,38, stack/scripts/armada-watchtower-e2e-job.py:12,30, env/gates/watchtower/helper.ts:8,24, env/gates/watchtower/watch.ts:13,28, and the job files armada-custodian-e2e, armada-custodian-frost, armada-env-verify, armada-nitro-e2e, armada-watchtower-e2e and armada-watchtower-scenario, each of which sets network_mode: host. Service-name uses (armada-fixturenet-geth:8545): docker-compose-armada-env-reconcile.yml:29,39. docker-compose-armada-watchtower-discrimination-e2e.yml and stack/scripts/armada-watchtower-discrimination-e2e-job.py do not use host networking; inside the job's own network namespace they bind 127.0.0.1:8545 to armada-fixturenet-geth:8545 (yml:7-19). The comment at docker-compose-armada-nitro-e2e.yml:4-6 states that lib/sdk/chain-config.ts in the image uses http://localhost:8545 for chain 31337. armada-nitro-deploy and armada-nitro-scenario name armada-nitro-anvil:8545 and belong to the separate armada-nitro anvil stack.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. 1. Read the network.ports block of ~/deployments/armada-fixturenet-e12/spec.yml and stack/scripts/fixturenet-new:113-116. 2. Run grep -n -E '(127\.0\.0\.1|localhost|armada-fixturenet-geth):(8545|8546|5052)' stack/compose-jobs/*.yml stack/scripts/* env/gates/watchtower/*.ts. 3. Run grep -l 'network_mode: host' stack/compose-jobs/*.yml.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) stack/scripts/fixturenet-new and the job files under stack/compose-jobs/"

payload.body: intake-escalation-reason: could not work out what to build for arn-e7a: The report is a forensic audit — grep hits across stack/compose-jobs/*.yml, stack/scripts/*, and env/gates/watchtower/*.ts, plus the shared fixturenet's generated spec.yml — not a stated defect with a stated fix. It never asserts a reproducible failure (e.g., a specific job observed reading the shared chain's state instead of its own); it only lists where port 8545/8546/5052 and host networking appear or do not appear. Acceptance criteria are explicitly marked 'pending' by the reporter, so there is no stated observable outcome to build an oracle against. Three open questions need a human answer before this is a buildable spec: (1) Is 'a full e2e run builds its own fixturenet' already-implemented behavior being audited for a latent port-collision bug against the shared fixturenet at ~/deployments/armada-fixturenet-e12, or is it new behavior that stack/scripts/fixturenet-new and the job files must be built to provide? The report's wording ('What must hold') reads as a requirement, but the audit evidence reads as a description of the status quo. (2) The job set reaches geth through three different mechanisms — network_mode: host against a fixed 127.0.0.1:8545 (fixturenet-new, fixturenet-base-snapshot, armada-watchtower-e2e.py, armada-watchtower-e2e-job.py, helper.ts, watch.ts, and five host-network job files), docker-compose service-name resolution (docker-compose-armada-env-reconcile.yml, armada-fixturenet-geth:8545), and a job-local network bridging 127.0.0.1:8545 to armada-fixturenet-geth:8545 (docker-compose-armada-watchtower-discrimination-e2e.yml). It is unclear whether the fix is one change applicable to all three, or three separate per-mechanism changes — which decides whether this is one deliverable or several. (3) Ports 8546 and 5052 are published by the generated spec (stack/scripts/fixturenet-new:113-116, via --map-ports-to-host localhost-same) but appear in none of the searched job or script files. A human needs to say whether these should be removed from the published-port set, or whether some currently-unidentified consumer is missing and needs to be found or built. Without answers to these three questions, any restatement clause either invents the missing conclusion or launders an unverified assumption into a checkable predicate, which the instructions rule out in favor of escalation.. Your request is filed, but I could not settle how to check it is done — run `exophial discuss arn-e7a` to talk it through together.

Operator answers, 2026-10-15. (1) This is new behavior to build. A full e2e run builds its own fixturenet from the tree under test and runs while the shared fixturenet at ~/deployments/armada-fixturenet-e12 keeps running. (2) It is one deliverable. No job uses network_mode: host. Each job runs on its own deployment's Compose network and receives the RPC URL http://armada-fixturenet-geth:8545 as configuration, as docker-compose-armada-env-reconcile.yml already does with RECONCILER_RPC_URL. CLIENT_RPC in lib/armada-poc/lib/sdk/chain-config.ts:48 (used by lib/sdk/init.ts, network.ts and index.ts) becomes configurable; lib/armada-poc is a submodule of https://github.com/ship-armada/armada-poc pinned at 532bc064, so that is a change in that repository and a new submodule pin. (3) No deployment pins host ports. stack/scripts/fixturenet-new uses a laconic-so random mapping (--map-ports-to-host any-variable-random or localhost-fixed-random) instead of localhost-same. A host script finds a deployment's published port with docker port. The host scripts that use 127.0.0.1:8545 are stack/scripts/fixturenet-new:30, stack/scripts/fixturenet-base-snapshot:29 and scripts/run-frost-keygen-check.py:36; the filed audit did not search the top-level scripts/ directory, and this answer adds that site.

criticality: negligible

goal: Make every end-to-end job in this repository reach only the chain of its own deployment, with no job pinned to a fixed host port or using host networking, while a full e2e run builds its own fixturenet and the shared fixturenet keeps running untouched.

restatement:
  Today, armada-nitro's e2e jobs find their chain by one of three different routes: a fixed host port (127.0.0.1:8545) reached through network_mode: host, a compose service name, or a job-local network bridge. The shared fixturenet at ~/deployments/armada-fixturenet-e12 publishes fixed host ports (8545, 8546, 5052) that nothing in the audited files actually reads for 8546 or 5052. The operator has decided this is new behavior to build, as one deliverable: every e2e job must stop using network_mode: host and must instead receive its own deployment's RPC endpoint as configuration, addressed by compose service name (the pattern docker-compose-armada-env-reconcile.yml already uses for RECONCILER_RPC_URL). The armada-poc submodule's hardcoded CLIENT_RPC must become configurable, delivered through a new submodule pin replacing the current pin 532bc064. No deployment may pin a fixed host port; stack/scripts/fixturenet-new must use laconic-so's random port mapping, and any host script that still needs a published port (fixturenet-new, fixturenet-base-snapshot, run-frost-keygen-check.py) must discover it with `docker port`. The end result: a full e2e run builds its own fixturenet from the tree under test and runs every job against it, the shared fixturenet keeps running the whole time undisturbed, and each job reaches only its own deployment's chain. If this isolation fails, the worst outcome is a confusing or wrong test result and a shared fixturenet that must be rebuilt with the existing fixturenet-new/fixturenet-recover scripts; no production system or irreplaceable data is at risk.

restatement_clauses:
- c1: stack/scripts/fixturenet-new must use a laconic-so random port mapping (--map-ports-to-host any-variable-random or localhost-fixed-random) instead of --map-ports-to-host localhost-same, so no deployment pins host ports.
- c2: A host script that needs a deployment's published port — stack/scripts/fixturenet-new:30, stack/scripts/fixturenet-base-snapshot:29, and scripts/run-frost-keygen-check.py:36 — must find that port with `docker port` instead of hardcoding 127.0.0.1:8545.
- c3: No e2e job must set network_mode: host; this removes it from the compose job files that set it today (armada-custodian-e2e, armada-custodian-frost, armada-env-verify, armada-nitro-e2e, armada-watchtower-e2e, armada-watchtower-scenario).
- c4: Each job must receive its chain RPC endpoint as configuration naming its own deployment's compose service, e.g. http://armada-fixturenet-geth:8545, the same pattern docker-compose-armada-env-reconcile.yml already uses for RECONCILER_RPC_URL.
- c5: CLIENT_RPC in lib/armada-poc/lib/sdk/chain-config.ts:48 must become configurable instead of fixed to http://localhost:8545, delivered through an updated armada-poc submodule and a new pin in this repo replacing the current pin 532bc064.
- c6: A full e2e run must build its own fixturenet from the tree under test and run every e2e job on that fixturenet, while the shared fixturenet at ~/deployments/armada-fixturenet-e12 keeps running throughout the run.
- c7: Each job must reach only the chain of its own deployment, and never the chain of the shared fixturenet at ~/deployments/armada-fixturenet-e12 or any other deployment.

acceptance_criteria:
- c1: The file stack/scripts/fixturenet-new no longer tells laconic-so to map ports to the same fixed host port.
- c1: The file stack/scripts/fixturenet-new now tells laconic-so to pick a random host port for each deployment.
- c2: Every one of the three host scripts that needs a deployment's port (fixturenet-new, fixturenet-base-snapshot, run-frost-keygen-check.py) now asks Docker for that port instead of assuming a fixed number.
- c2: None of the three host scripts above still hardcodes the fixed address 127.0.0.1:8545.
- c3: No compose file for an e2e job in stack/compose-jobs still runs the job on the host's own network.
- c4: Every one of the six e2e job compose files now points at its own chain by the compose service name armada-fixturenet-geth on port 8545, the same way the existing env-reconcile job already does.
- c5: The armada-poc chain configuration file no longer has the chain address fixed to http://localhost:8545.
- c5: The armada-poc submodule now points at a commit other than the old pin 532bc064.
- c6: Starting a full e2e run builds a brand-new fixturenet from the current code, runs the e2e jobs on it, and the separate shared fixturenet at ~/deployments/armada-fixturenet-e12 is still running, before and after, without interruption.
- c7: While one e2e job runs on its own freshly built fixturenet, the separate shared fixturenet receives zero new chain requests from that job.

  Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) armada-nitro forge suite (test/)

criticality: negligible

goal: Make `forge test` itself fail if the adjudicator ever imports ERC-4626 or calls an exchange-rate function, instead of relying on a script forge test never runs.

restatement:
  The armada-nitro forge test suite must itself enforce, by running real code, the rule that the adjudicator stays free of ERC-4626 exchange-rate machinery. Today that rule is checked only by the standalone script scripts/check-settlement-rate-free.py, which scans src/ArmadaNitroAdjudicator.sol and src/nitro/ for ERC4626, IERC4626, convertToAssets, convertToShares, and preview. forge test does not call that script, so a `forge test` run gives no signal on this rule at all; a future change could reintroduce one of those names into the adjudicator or the Nitro framework source and the forge suite would still pass. The fix must add a forge test that performs this same source check and fails the suite when a forbidden name is present, so that `forge test` alone is sufficient to catch a violation. The rule itself — that the adjudicator and Nitro source presently contain none of these names — already holds at commit d51ae19 and must keep holding.

restatement_clauses:
- c1: src/ArmadaNitroAdjudicator.sol and every .sol file under src/nitro/ contain none of ERC4626, IERC4626, convertToAssets, convertToShares, or preview.
- c2: Running `forge test` executes a check for this rule and fails the suite when a forbidden name is present in that source, so the forge suite is itself the enforcement, not an unexercised side script.

acceptance_criteria:
- c1: The adjudicator contract file and every file in the Nitro framework source contain no mention of ERC4626, IERC4626, convertToAssets, convertToShares, or preview.
- c2: Running `forge test` passes against the real adjudicator source, but as soon as a forbidden name like convertToAssets is added to a scratch copy of that source and the suite is pointed at it, `forge test` fails. This shows the forge suite is the thing actually catching the violation, not a script it never calls.

criticality: marginal

goal: Fix WatchtowerScenario.s.sol's respond() so its per-asset fallback pays every asset index in the channel's outcome, not only index 0, when concludeAndTransferAllAssets reverts.

restatement:
  The watchtower script must pay out every asset of a finalized channel, even when a different asset's payout transfer reverts. Today, WatchtowerScenario.s.sol's respond() function falls back to conclude plus one transfer call, with assetIndex fixed at 0, whenever concludeAndTransferAllAssets would revert. No call in respond() pays any asset index other than 0. So an asset at index 1 or higher, whose own transfer would succeed, stays unpaid whenever the fallback path runs. The fix must make respond() call adjudicator.transfer(assetIndex, ...) for every asset index in the channel's outcome, not only index 0.

restatement_clauses:
- c1: Each asset of a finalized channel exits, even when a different asset's payout reverts.
- c2: When concludeAndTransferAllAssets would revert, respond() calls adjudicator.transfer(assetIndex, ...) for every asset index in the channel's outcome, not only assetIndex 0.

criticality: marginal

goal: Give settleStale (scenario B of script/WatchtowerScenario.s.sol) the same per-asset transfer(assetIndex, ...) fallback that respond already has, so a second asset's reverting token can no longer block payout of a working first asset.

restatement:
  Design document 15 states invariant I5. Invariant I5 says each asset of a finalized channel must exit, even when another asset's payout reverts. Task E16 names this as deliverable S4: the watchtower and the e2e gate must fall back to a per-asset transfer(assetIndex, ...) call when transferAllAssets reverts. The respond function in script/WatchtowerScenario.s.sol already has this fallback. The settleStale function (scenario B) does not. settleStale calls only adjudicator.transferAllAssets. On a two-asset channel where the second asset's token reverts on transfer, after the challenge window elapses, settleStale(0) exits 1 and pays nothing, including the first asset whose token works fine. The fix must give settleStale the same per-asset fallback respond already has. After the fix, running settleStale on that same two-asset channel must succeed and must pay the first asset. The amount paid to the first asset must equal the amount it would receive if the second asset's token did not revert, so the fix removes only the failure, not any part of the correct payout.

- c1: On a two-asset channel whose second asset's token reverts on transfer, after openAndChallenge(0) and the challenge window, running `forge script script/WatchtowerScenario.s.sol --sig 'settleStale(uint256)' 0 --broadcast` must exit 0 and pay the channel's first asset a non-zero amount, not exit 1 as it does now.
- c2: The first asset's paid amount from that settlement must equal the first asset's paid amount when the second asset's token does not revert (script/WatchtowerPerAssetSetup.s.sol's setup(false)), so the fallback changes only whether the settlement succeeds, not how much the first asset is paid.

criticality: negligible

goal: Make the watchtower's respond() and settleStale() scenarios always pay every asset of a finalized channel through its own transfer(assetIndex, ...) call, remove their trial-then-fallback dependency on concludeAndTransferAllAssets and transferAllAssets, and update the e2e job script's broadcast check to match.

restatement:
  The watchtower scenario script and the e2e gate must pay every asset of a finalized channel with its own separate transfer(assetIndex, ...) call. No payout step may depend on, or try, the combined functions transferAllAssets or concludeAndTransferAllAssets. No script may attempt one payout function first and fall back to a different payout function when the first attempt fails. Today, respond() in script/WatchtowerScenario.s.sol (lines 156-220) tries concludeAndTransferAllAssets on a throwaway state copy first. It broadcasts that combined call if the trial succeeds. If the trial fails, respond() calls conclude() and then tries transfer(i, ...) on a throwaway copy for each asset, broadcasting only the calls that succeeded. settleStale() (lines 258-296) tries transferAllAssets on a throwaway copy first and broadcasts it if that trial succeeds. If the trial fails, settleStale() broadcasts transfer(0, ...) for asset index 0 only, and never attempts the other asset indexes. stack/scripts/armada-watchtower-e2e-job.py (line 133) reads the respond() broadcast by looking for a transaction whose function name starts with concludeAndTransferAllAssets(. That check will stop matching once respond() stops broadcasting the combined call, so the job script must check for the per-asset transfer calls instead. The fix removes the trial-then-fallback logic from respond() and settleStale(), makes each function always pay through transfer(assetIndex, ...) for every asset, and updates the e2e job script's check to match. This is scenario and e2e-gate script hardening (docs/tasks/E16-adjudicator-hardening.md, S4): its worst failure is a wrong or flaky e2e signal about watchtower payout behavior, not a loss of custody over live user funds.

restatement_clauses:

- settlestale-per-asset-payout: settleStale() in script/WatchtowerScenario.s.sol pays every asset of a finalized channel with its own transfer(assetIndex, ...) call for every asset index, not only asset index 0, and never broadcasts a transferAllAssets call as its payout, whether or not that combined call would have succeeded.
- e2e-job-removes-combined-check: stack/scripts/armada-watchtower-e2e-job.py no longer checks the respond() broadcast for a transaction whose function starts with concludeAndTransferAllAssets(.
- e2e-job-adds-per-asset-check: stack/scripts/armada-watchtower-e2e-job.py checks the respond() broadcast for per-asset transfer(assetIndex, ...) calls instead of the combined-payout call.

acceptance_criteria:

- settlestale-per-asset-payout: Finalize a two-asset channel and run the watchtower's settleStale() step twice: once under conditions where a single combined payout covering both assets would have gone through, and once where it would not. payload.description:
Request:
  What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. The armada-sdk disclosure checker (ship-armada/armada-sdk#142, src/disclosure/checker.ts) accepts a disclosure package built from a real armada-nitro fixturenet run. Every chain event that the checker reads comes from a real transaction. The run covers one chain of custody. Hop H1: a test EOA shields USDC into the pool. Hops H2 and H4: the wallet spends that note through depositFromNote into a hub channel. Hop H5: the channel concludes with a SHIELD payout to a fresh note of the same wallet. Hop H6: the wallet unshields that note to a second test EOA. A copy of the package with one hop changed fails the checker, and the checker names the failed check.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. The disclosure tests in armada-sdk PR #142 use real Groth16 disclosure proofs. Every chain event in those tests is a synthetic fixture that the test computes to match the proofs. No hop is checked against an event from a real transaction. The SDK has no decoder for armada-nitro logs (Deposited, the finalized channel outcome). The armada-nitro-e2e gate already shields USDC and funds two channels with real-proof depositFromNote calls (env/gates/nitro-e2e/prepare.ts, script/FixturenetScenario.s.sol). That gate does not unshield the payout note to an EOA. It does not record the events in a form that the SDK checker reads.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run the new capture job on the fixturenet. The job writes one fixture file: for each hop, the transaction hash, the receipt and the decoded events, plus the test-wallet data that the SDK builder needs (keys, note randoms, tree number and leaf index). The job then builds a disclosure package with the armada-sdk builder and runs the armada-sdk checker on it: the checker returns a pass. The job changes one recorded value in a copy (for example the payout npk, the channelId or one nullifier) and runs the checker again: the checker returns a fail with the named check.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Use real proofs, real contracts and real transactions. Do not mock or compute chain events. Use the dev disclosure-circuit artifacts from ship-armada/armada-circuits#3 (build/disclosure/ in armada-circuits: main_disclosure.wasm, final.zkey, vkey.json); they are an unsafe dev setup for tests only. Use throwaway test-wallet keys only. Do not change the pool, the disclosure circuit or the adjudicator. Use armada-sdk from branch selective-disclosure (PR #142) as an external dependency; do not copy its code into armada-nitro. The fixture format is the one that src/disclosure/chain-source.ts in armada-sdk reads. If that format cannot represent an armada-nitro log, record the gap in the handoff and do not invent a format. The waUSDC swap of armada-laconic design page 16 depends on task E11 (armada-assets-e2e); this filing covers the USDC chain only. Design: armada-laconic engineering/16-selective-disclosure.md and ADR-0020.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) armada-nitro fixturenet gate jobs: env/gates/, stack/compose-jobs/, script/. New capture job beside armada-nitro-e2e.
Points: 8

  Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) src/nitro/MultiAssetHolder.sol, function _transferAsset, line 461

criticality: critical

goal: An ERC20 payout from the adjudicator moves the tokens to the destination, or the call reverts. The adjudicator never records a payout that did not move the tokens.

restatement:
  When the adjudicator pays an ERC20 asset out of a channel to an external destination, the payout must have only two possible results. Either the destination receives the full amount of tokens, or the whole call reverts and the channel holdings stay unchanged. Now, src/nitro/MultiAssetHolder.sol:461 in _transferAsset calls IERC20(asset).transfer(destination, amount) and ignores the returned bool. The adjudicator decrements the channel holdings before this call. Thus a token that returns false moves no tokens, but the call succeeds and the beneficiary loses the entitlement. The E16 brief (docs/tasks/E16-adjudicator-hardening.md:31) requires SafeERC20 for every token call. The fix makes the payout use SafeERC20, so that a false return reverts the payout. The fix also keeps payouts working for a token that returns no value, which SafeERC20 accepts.

restatement_clauses:
- c1: A payout of an ERC20 asset from the adjudicator moves the tokens to the destination, or the call reverts: when the token's transfer returns false, the payout call reverts and the channel holdings and the destination balance do not change.
- c2: _transferAsset in src/nitro/MultiAssetHolder.sol (line 461) uses SafeERC20 for the ERC20 transfer, as the E16 brief (docs/tasks/E16-adjudicator-hardening.md:31) requires for every token call: a token whose transfer returns true, or returns no value, pays the full amount to the destination, and the channel holdings fall by the same amount.

payload.description:
Request:
  What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. A committed script, stack/scripts/armada-disclosure-capture.py, runs one selective-disclosure chain of custody on the armada-nitro fixturenet as real transactions, and writes the result as files. The worker writes and commits the script; the script, not the worker, performs every step. One run writes two files into a run directory given by --out: fixture.json and report.json. The chain: H1, a test EOA shields USDC into the pool. H2 and H4, the wallet spends that note through depositFromNote into a hub channel. H7, the wallet and the hub co-sign channel states, the hub through its HubCustodian delegate. H5, the channel concludes with a SHIELD payout to a fresh note of the same wallet. H6, the wallet unshields that note to a second test EOA. fixture.json holds, for each hop, the transaction hash, the receipt, the decoded events with the emitting chain id and contract address, the co-signed channel states with every signature and the block at which the hub delegate signed, and the test-wallet data that the armada-sdk builder needs. The script fails at the first error: it exits non-zero, writes report.json with the name of the failed step and the error, and does not retry. A timeout counts as an error.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. No script records a real disclosure chain. The armada-sdk disclosure checker (draft PR ship-armada/armada-sdk#142, branch selective-disclosure on the fork AFDudley/armada-sdk, head 0aa2ba1) has tests with synthetic chain events only. Its hub EIP-1271 check has tests with a stand-in predicate only, and no test calls a live HubCustodian. The armada-nitro-e2e gate shields USDC and funds channels with real-proof depositFromNote calls (env/gates/nitro-e2e/prepare.ts, script/FixturenetScenario.s.sol). That gate writes no file that the SDK reads, and it does not unshield the payout note. arn-026 described this work and is closed.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run the script once against the running fixturenet with --out <dir>. It exits 0 and writes fixture.json and report.json. The checks then read those files and do not rerun the capture. Check 1, independent of the script: for every transaction hash in fixture.json, cast receipt against the fixturenet RPC returns status 1, and the events in the receipt equal the recorded events. Check 2, independent of the script's checking logic: stack/scripts/armada-disclosure-verify.mjs loads fixture.json, builds the package with the armada-sdk builder, and calls the armada-sdk checker with a chain source that reads the fixturenet RPC, including isValidSignature on the live HubCustodian. It holds no checking logic of its own. It reports a pass. Check 3: the same verify script, on copies of the package with one value changed (the payout npk, the channelId, one nullifier, one channel-state allocation, one event's chain id, one event's contract address), reports a fail and the name of the failed check each time. Check 4, error handling: run the capture with an RPC URL that nothing listens on, then with a missing circuit-artifact directory, then with an armada-sdk path that does not exist. Each run exits non-zero within 60 seconds, and report.json names the failed step.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Real proofs, real contracts and real transactions only. Do not mock or compute chain events. Use the dev disclosure-circuit artifacts from ship-armada/armada-circuits#3 (build/disclosure/ in an armada-circuits checkout: main_disclosure_js/main_disclosure.wasm, final.zkey, vkey.json); they are an unsafe dev setup for tests only. goal: Bump the lib/armada-poc pin to 5d076c4eb9f27dd931d6c0b392b92cd850cb66d5 and keep the build, tests and pre-commit gate green.

restatement:
  The armada-nitro repository must pin its lib/armada-poc submodule to armada-poc integrated commit 5d076c4eb9f27dd931d6c0b392b92cd850cb66d5, not 2db1d33. That commit carries the M8 privacy pool and its Snark Groth16 library at contracts/privacy-pool/types/SnarkTypes.sol, so a channel app can reuse a standalone Groth16 checker. After the bump, forge build, forge test and the pre-commit gate must all pass. Only the files that import the pool may change, and only as far as the bump needs. These are test/helpers/ArmadaFixture.sol, test/helpers/ArmadaNotes.sol, test/ArmadaNitroAdjudicator.t.sol and the scripts under script/. The vendored src/nitro stays untouched. No second Groth16 verifier is added.

restatement_clauses:
- c1: git ls-tree HEAD lib/armada-poc shows the gitlink equal to 5d076c4eb9f27dd931d6c0b392b92cd850cb66d5, not 2db1d33.
- c2: git -C lib/armada-poc cat-file -e HEAD:contracts/privacy-pool/types/SnarkTypes.sol exits 0.
- c3: forge build exits 0.
- c4: forge test exits 0 and its summary reports 0 failed.
- c5: pre-commit run --all-files passes, and the forge-test hook prints Passed.
- c6: src/nitro (vendored go-nitro) has no changes.
- c7: No second Groth16 verifier is added. The M8 pool Snark library is reused.

acceptance_criteria:
- c1: The recorded submodule version for lib/armada-poc is exactly 5d076c4eb9f27dd931d6c0b392b92cd850cb66d5.
- c2: The pinned armada-poc checkout contains the Snark library file SnarkTypes.sol under the privacy-pool types folder.
- c3: The full contract build finishes with no errors after the pin change.
- c4: The full contract test run finishes and reports zero failed tests.
- c5: The pre-commit run over all files succeeds and the forge-test hook reports Passed.
- c6: No file under src/nitro differs from the main branch.
- c7: The count of Groth16 verifier contracts or verifyProof functions defined in armada-nitro's own tests, helpers and scripts is zero.

A heldValue(asset, channelId) view returns 0 for an empty commitment, else pool.preimageOf(commitment).value. Every reader of the old amount uses heldValue. The base deposit entry point is removed from the adjudicator and IMultiAssetHolder (a channel is funded only through depositFromNote, which carries a proof). forge build and the whole forge test suite pass. What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. MultiAssetHolder.holdings maps (asset, channelId) to a uint256 raw balance, and ArmadaNitroAdjudicator exposes deposit, a raw ERC-20 transfer in. The channel collateral is a token balance held by the adjudicator, not a pool note.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. A test prints one JSON line. heldValue_empty=0: an unset (asset, channelId) returns 0. heldValue_set equals the preimage value: a (asset, channelId) whose commitment a mock preimageOf maps to a fixed CommitmentPreimage returns that preimage's value. deposit_selector_present=false: a low-level call to the old IMultiAssetHolder.deposit 4-byte selector on ArmadaNitroAdjudicator reaches a missing function, not a revert. forge build exits 0. The full forge test suite reports failed=0.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. heldValue always reads through pool.preimageOf, never a cached or passed-in amount. No code path sets holdings to a commitment the adjudicator did not verify (that is N1b/N2a). heldValue's 0-for-empty branch is not a real 0-value note. Add preimageOf and transactOwned to src/armada/IArmadaPool.sol. Keep SafeCast for the pool uint120 values and an event for every holdings change. Request:

State the invariant or expectation this concerns. stack/scripts/armada-disclosure-acceptance.py runs the selective-disclosure chain of custody end to end on a fresh per-run fixturenet. It creates the fixturenet with stack/scripts/fixturenet-new and a run-unique name (TMPDIR set to the repo .scratch), then runs hops H1-H7 of docs/tasks/16-selective-disclosure.md as real transactions: H1 a test EOA shields USDC; H2 and H4 the note funds a hub channel through depositFromNote; H7 the wallet and the hub co-sign channel states; H5 the channel pays a SHIELD payout to a fresh note of the same wallet; H6 that note is unshielded to a second test EOA. It records every transaction and event into a disclosure package file, then tears the fixturenet down. A docker-compose job under stack/compose-jobs/ runs this script.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. No stack/scripts/armada-disclosure-acceptance.py exists. No selective-disclosure compose job exists under stack/compose-jobs/. The hops are not run anywhere as one end-to-end chain.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run the selective-disclosure compose job. The script prints one JSON line with the fields hops_ok (true when H1, H2, H4, H5, H6 and H7 each succeeded on the fixturenet), eoa2_usdc_delta (a positive integer, the USDC the second EOA gained), eoa_distinct (true when the second EOA differs from the shielding EOA), payout_note_owned (true when the payout note npk derives from the shielding wallet masterPublicKey), and package_path (the written disclosure package). The same run creates the fixturenet and then tears it down.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. The run changes no pool contract, no disclosure circuit and no adjudicator contract. The fixturenet name is unique per run. The script does not depend on a pre-existing shared fixturenet.

Request:
  What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. stack/scripts/armada-disclosure-acceptance.py calls the armada-sdk disclosure checker from the installed AFDudley/armada-sdk fork (branch selective-disclosure, commit 0aa2ba1, draft PR ship-armada/armada-sdk#142) on the recorded package, with a chain source that reads the fixturenet. The checker passes with no failed checks. Each hub signature is checked by isValidSignature on the HubCustodian deployed on the fixturenet, which returns 0x1626ba7e. A copy of the package with exactly one recorded value changed (the payout npk, the channelId, one nullifier, one channel-state allocation, one event chain id, or one event contract address) is rejected, and the checker names the failed check each time. The gate job run with an RPC that nothing listens on, and again with an RPC that accepts but never answers, each stops with a non-zero exit within 60 seconds and names the failed step, tried once only.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. The harness records the package but does not call the SDK checker, does not do tamper rejection, and does not handle a bad RPC. The armada-sdk disclosure checker is not installed or invoked.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. The script prints one JSON line with the fields checker_pass (true when the checker passes the real package with no failed checks), hub_sig_1271 (true when each hub signature returns 0x1626ba7e from isValidSignature on the fixturenet HubCustodian), tamper_rejections (the integer 6, one per changed value, each naming its failed check), sdk_fork_commit (the installed armada-sdk resolves to 0aa2ba1), and sdk_source_absent (true when no SDK disclosure source file is copied into the armada-nitro tree). The two bad-RPC runs each exit non-zero within 60 seconds and name the failed step.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. The checker comes from the installed armada-sdk package, not from a copy in armada-nitro. restatement:
  The forge_mutation_gated_test check mutates a changed Solidity source file one token at a time and reruns the named forge test against each mutant. A mutant that the test does not catch is counted as MISSED, and any MISSED mutant makes the check fail. The request is that a mutant whose write leaves the source file's content byte-for-byte the same as the original is not a real mutant. Such a mutant must not be counted as missed, and it must not make a forge_mutation_gated_test check fail. A real mutant, whose content differs from the original and which the test does not catch, must still be counted as missed and must still make the check fail. The trigger was armada-nitro pebble arn-451, where 5 of 6 clauses failed with missed-mutant details that all read 'MISSED (No files changed, compilation skipped'. payload.description:
Request:
  What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. The same fixturenet run continues the Baal governance lifecycle against the real G1 to G7a contracts. A pool spend moves value through PrivacyPool.transact using the armada-sdk planSpend and prove flow. A majority of ARM voting power casts a hostile Baal proposal to drain the treasury without executing it. During that proposal a holder calls ShieldedRagequit.ragequit and exits with the correct pro-rata share. In a second run the hostile proposal executes, and ragequit still succeeds afterward at the new smaller treasury balance. A captured majority cannot block an exit.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. No gate runs a pool spend, a hostile vote, or a ragequit today. The armada-nitro-e2e gate and G7a stop after the claim and one vote. No step exercises ShieldedRagequit on the fixturenet, and no step proves a ragequit exit succeeds during or after a hostile proposal.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run the extended armada-nitro-e2e gate (G7a then G7b) on a fresh fixturenet. After the run read live chain state. One: a real PrivacyPool.transact spend verifies on chain (spend_verified true). Two: the hostile proposal is recorded but does not block the ragequit (proposal_recorded true, ragequit_blocked false). Three: the ragequit payout equals the bound G3 S4 enforces, both before the hostile proposal executes and after it executes at the smaller balance (payout_matches_bound_before true, payout_matches_bound_after true). The run fails before G7b exists and passes once the spend, hostile-vote, ragequit, and post-execution steps are wired.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Extends G7a and the existing armada-nitro-e2e gate, it does not replace them or add a new fixturenet harness. Fixturenet first, no Sepolia or mainnet. The spend uses the armada-sdk planSpend and prove flow, the same shape the gate already proves for channel funding. The negative case runs a real Baal execute call against the real spend path, not a stand-in that assumes the drain. It runs against the real fixturenet contracts, not a Baal or Safe mock.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) armada-nitro env/gates/nitro-e2e, extending G7a scenario script beside script/LocalScenario.s.sol
Points: 5

In the redeem scenario the hub redeems its waUSDC for USDC and its USDC balance grows by at least the yield scenario principal. A run without the borrow makes the yield check fail. Before stack/scripts/fixturenet-new creates a deployment, it removes any earlier deployment that it left and that no live process uses. It finds earlier deployments by the exact deployment name prefix. It guards the deployment path so it never acts on an empty or unset path. For each stale deployment it runs laconic-so deployment stop --delete-volumes and then removes the deployment directory. A deployment that an earlier run left after a SIGKILL is cleaned by the next run that shares the name prefix.
  What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. stack/scripts/fixturenet-new creates a deployment without first removing earlier deployments it left. A run that a SIGKILL ended leaves its deployment. The next run does not clean it.

A cleanup step runs before the deploy create step. The cleanup step runs laconic-so deployment stop --delete-volumes. The cleanup step guards its path against an empty value. The cleanup step selects deployments by the exact name prefix. After fixturenet-new runs with a stale same-prefix deployment left on disk, that stale deployment is gone.
  What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. The cleanup step guards the deployment path against an empty value. The cleanup step acts only on the exact name prefix. The cleanup step does not remove a deployment that a live process uses.

criticality: negligible

goal: fixturenet-new cleans up stale same-prefix deployments before it creates a new deployment.

restatement:

It finds those deployments by the exact deployment name prefix. It guards the deployment path so it never acts on an empty or unset path. For each stale deployment it runs laconic-so deployment stop --delete-volumes and then removes the deployment directory. This means a deployment left by a run that a SIGKILL ended is cleaned by the next run that shares the name prefix.

Then waUSDC.convertToAssets(1e6) and the Aave USDC liquidityIndex must both increase. In the redeem scenario the hub redeems its waUSDC for USDC, and its USDC balance must grow by at least the yield scenario principal. A run without the borrow must make the yield check fail. The command grep -n pool.shield src/ArmadaNitroAdjudicator.sol returns nothing. The full forge test suite compiles and passes.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. There is no protocol fee on a payout (operator ruling 2026-10-22): a payout is a plain output with no fee tag and no cumulativeFees coupling. payload.description:
Request:
  What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. Two runs of fixturenet-new on the same armada-nitro commit compute the same base cache key, so a base snapshot written by one run is restored by the next run on the warm path. The key depends only on the committed sources, not on the host python version and not on local build output.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. On one armada-nitro commit, with env/reconciler files git-unchanged (last commit 2026-09-30, clean working tree), stack/scripts/base-key.py piped to sha256sum then cut to 16 hex produced: with python 3.12.3, 5a47353c5b21cd7d; with python 3.14.3, dde2799b6ae48521. At an earlier time on the same commit, python 3.14.3 produced d1d7469b02423dee; between that time and now the cerc/armada-nitro-env stage image IDs changed while the env/reconciler files stayed identical. deployments/.snapshots holds two base snapshot key files, fdaad8d29e3f6615 and 4c66d5314e294fd0; the current base-key computation equals neither.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run stack/scripts/base-key.py --root . piped to sha256sum then cut -c1-16, first with python 3.12.3 then with python 3.14.3; the keys differ on the same commit. Run a cold fixturenet-new, then recompute with the same python; the key differs again. Compare the current computation to the .key files in deployments/.snapshots; it matches neither fdaad8d29e3f6615 nor 4c66d5314e294fd0.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. The d5a acceptance must still stand up the real fixturenet; it must not be weakened.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) stack/scripts/base-key.py, which calls docker image inspect for local image IDs at line 109 and hashes python ast output; used by stack/scripts/fixturenet-base-common.sh compute_base_key and stack/scripts/fixturenet-new
Points: 6

- stack/scripts/fixturenet-new @ cbf8680b53e40f20eb873fbd499a428a7794ebc8: chosen by whether a snapshot exists for the computed cache key

- acceptance criteria pending

goal: All deployed armada-nitro contracts are at or below 24,576 bytes of runtime code, and the pre-commit gate fails when a contract exceeds that limit.

restatement:
  In the armada-nitro repo, every non-test contract that a deploy script deploys must have a runtime size of 24,576 bytes or less (the EIP-170 limit). Today ArmadaNitroAdjudicator is 25,558 bytes, 982 bytes over the limit. Because of this, forge build --sizes fails and the fixturenet deploy (forge script script/Deploy.s.sol:Deploy) fails at the EVM CREATE size check. The work must bring ArmadaNitroAdjudicator, and every other deployed contract, to or below 24,576 bytes. The work must also make the repository gate (pre-commit run --all-files) check contract sizes, so that the gate fails when a contract is above the limit.

- c1: forge build --sizes exits 0, and every non-test contract, including ArmadaNitroAdjudicator, has a Runtime Size at or below 24,576 bytes (Runtime Margin >= 0).
